title: SIRO: Empowering Version Compatibility in Intermediate Representations via Program Synthesis
problem: Different versions of LLVM IR create incompatibility issues that prevent IR-based tools like static analyzers from functioning across systems with different LLVM versions. Manual translation between IR versions is labor-intensive.
motivation: IR version incompatibility blocks deployment of static analyzers and security tools across diverse environments, limiting their practical impact on real-world systems.
method: Siro uses a divide-and-conquer algorithm skeleton to decompose IR translation tasks. Program synthesis automatically generates translators for individual IR instructions by searching implementation spaces. The framework produces complete IR version converters that handle instruction-level transformations between LLVM versions.
key_novelty: Automated program synthesis of IR version translators that eliminates manual implementation effort and enables rapid generation of IR adapters across version boundaries.
contributions: Generic divide-and-conquer algorithm skeleton for IR translation tasks
Program synthesis framework for automatic IR instruction translator generation
Ten functional LLVM IR translators for different version pairs, each developed in under three hours
Practical deployment discovering 80 new Linux kernel vulnerabilities through improved static analysis

metrics.other: 80 new Linux kernel vulnerabilities discovered, <3 hours per translator

primary_theme: automated IR version translation via program synthesis
